claude.rationale: This is a whole-company, all-cash going-private reverse triangular merger: the entire corporate entity survived intact as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Parent ("the entire corporate entity, not a carved-out business unit, was the transaction's subject"), so product (T4), operational processes (T5), and organization/people (T6) all crossed the ownership boundary together as an intact going concern — no product-vs-process carve-out (gap_45=0). The people/organization tier moved coherently with operations, reinforced by 18-month compensation/benefit continuity and six-year D&O indemnification carried across closing, so no process-vs-organization mismatch (gap_56=0). Owner intent is coded replace because a financial sponsor (Pamplona) installed new controlling ownership via newly formed Parent/Merger Sub and public equity ownership was fully cashed out at $88.10/share.

grok.rationale: The deal is a whole-company reverse triangular merger in which Merger Sub merged into PAREXEL and PAREXEL survived as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Parent, so the entire corporate entity—not a carved-out unit—was the subject; product/services and the operational processes that produce them therefore crossed together with no structural product-vs-process mismatch at closing (gap_45=0). Organization/people likewise transferred with the surviving entity, reinforced by contractual 18-month employee compensation/benefit continuity and severance-guideline assumption plus six-year D&O indemnification, so processes and organization were aligned at closing (gap_56=0); no transitional-services gap-mitigation instrument was required or documented.

openai.rationale: The entire corporate entity, rather than a carved-out business unit, transferred to Parent, with PAREXEL surviving as its wholly owned subsidiary; the slice describes PAREXEL's clinical-research, consulting, communications, and technology offerings together with its global operating footprint, so no product-versus-process separation is documented at closing. The whole-company transfer also carried the existing organization across the boundary, reinforced by contractual 18-month compensation, benefits, and severance continuity for continuing employees; therefore, no process-versus-organization mismatch is documented at closing.
